title: Edge dropout causing prefix duplication and orphaned streaming sessions — incident triage & fix
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported duplicate early tokens followed by truncated final output when a streaming connection crossed an edge instance boundary (LB -> edge -> origin) during a short outage or pod restart. The end-user sees repeated prefix text, then silence or a partial finalization event. This started after the kernel scheduling change in runtime-1.20 (see telemetry correlations).

Goal: Ship a targeted fix that prevents duplicate-prefix emission and provides deterministic resume semantics for hosted SSE clients; deploy a short-term mitigation (session fencing + conservative idle GC) while longer validation (concurrency kernel revert or patch) lands.

Scope: Hosted API streaming only for tenants routed via the multi-edge LB (not Dedicated private plane). Affects both SDK and raw SSE clients that rely on resume semantics or receive chunked tokens.

Immediate customer impact: Several PLG customers observed truncated transcripts during long generation tasks and have opened escalations (support tickets S-10092, S-10102). Revenue risk for 2 customers in evaluation stage.
repro_steps: 1) Initiate a long-generation streaming request (~> 4000 token target) against hosted endpoint from client behind a simulated flaky path.
2) Introduce a short TCP reset on the active edge pod (30–1500 ms) while server is mid-stream flushing token batches.
3) Client re-connects and requests resume using session id; observe duplicated tokens for the last batch and then finalization never arrives or final message truncated.
4) Repro is most reliable when batch flush interval = 40–120ms and KV cache eviction occurs during the outage window.
telemetry_findings: Spike in stream re-connects correlated with edge pod churn times (kube rolling updates) — nodes with kernel scheduling patch had 2x more partial-writes before restart.
Chunk-level checksums absent in production path for older clients -> impossible to detect duplicate vs missing chunk without session fencing metadata.
Observed cases where origin accepted replayed request and emitted the same token batch again because session token map was not fenced at edge handoff.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Enable session-fence feature flag at edge to reject replayed resume attempts if session epoch mismatches. Deploy to canary tenants immediately.
2) Increase minimum idle stream GC timeout on edges from 5s -> 20s for canary to reduce premature eviction during flakiness windows.
3) Add temporary customer-facing advisory and suggested SDK patch (recommend exponential backoff + idempotent session-id refresh).
long_term_fix_plan: A) Patch runtime kernel scheduling path to guarantee atomic chunk flushes under pod drain (lead: infra-kernel team).
B) Introduce per-chunk 32-bit checksum and monotonic sequence markers at the protocol layer to allow safe de-duplication during resume (lead: serving-runtime).
C) Add a server-side reconciliation job that detects orphaned sessions and marks them tombstoned only after durable commit observed (lead: storage/kv).
D) Expand end-to-end test harness to simulate edge handoffs and perform deterministic replay checks as part of CI.
current_actions: Patch: Feature-flag 'edge-session-fence' rolled out to canary (region us-west-2) 2025-02-20 -> observed no duplicate-prefix reports for canary tenants.
Hotfix: Edge GC extended in canary clusters 2025-02-22; telemetry shows 48% reduction in orphaned session eviction events.
PR: draft PR opened for per-chunk checksum implementation — github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13742
Customer comms: Support drafted mitigation steps and customer-facing KB article linked in links.
risks: Session-fence stricter semantics may cause some legitimate resume attempts to be rejected if clients mis-handle session tokens; requires SDK updates and communication.
Kernel scheduling patch is invasive; reverting affects other performance gains. Need careful benchmarking vs correctness trade-off.
Proposed checksum adds ~12 bytes metadata per chunk — negligible CPU cost but increases network accounting; product sign-off required.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Coordinate SDK release that gracefully rotates session ids and exposes resume diagnostics (owner: client-sdk team).
2) Expand observability: add chunk-checksum health metric and per-tenant session-orphan rate dashboard (owner: console-team).
3) Run a controlled canary of kernel revert vs kernel patch and record end-to-end latency/cost regression (owner: infra-reliability).
4) Create automated post-incident report and circulate to GTM for impacted customer outreach (owner: Asha Patel).
notes: Product decision: prefer conservative correctness (no duplicate tokens) over aggressive perf tweak until checksum + reconciliation proved in staging.
Engineering tradeoff: add protocol metadata now and optimize size later; this is a one-time migration for hosted stream stability.
